subject: general
question: What was the life expectancy in India in 1947?
solution:
The correct answer is __**31 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Life expectancy** refers to the average number of years a person is expected to live based on current mortality rates.
 
• In **1947**, at the time of India's independence, the **life expectancy** was extremely low, averaging around **31 years**.
 
• This low figure reflected the poor socioeconomic conditions, widespread poverty, lack of healthcare facilities, and limited access to education during colonial rule.
 
• Several factors contributed to the low life expectancy, such as high rates of **infant mortality**, malnutrition, and infectious diseases like malaria and tuberculosis.
 
• Post-independence, the government of India began investing in public health infrastructure, reducing mortality rates, and improving overall life expectancy over the decades.
 
• The life expectancy at birth in India has shown significant improvement since 1947, increasing to over **70 years** as of 2023, due to advancements in healthcare, sanitation, and education.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is 31 years.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Factors Influencing Life Expectancy in 1947:**

 
 
• **Poverty:** A significant portion of India's population lived in poverty during the pre-independence and immediate post-independence periods. This limited access to basic resources like nutritious food and clean drinking water.
 
• **Healthcare:** India lacked proper healthcare facilities, medical infrastructure, and trained personnel during this time, leading to high mortality rates.
 
• **Diseases:** Epidemics of diseases such as cholera, malaria, and tuberculosis were rampant due to inadequate sanitation and lack of public health awareness.
 
• **Infant Mortality:** The infant mortality rate was extremely high, as many infants did not survive beyond their first year of life due to malnutrition and lack of medical care.
 
 
 
• **Life Expectancy Trends Post-1947:**
 
 
• Post-independence, India focused on improving public health through initiatives such as the **National Health Mission**, vaccination programs, and investments in rural healthcare.
 
• The introduction of **family planning** and awareness programs contributed to controlling population growth and improving living conditions.
 
• The creation of infrastructure like hospitals, sanitation systems, and access to clean drinking water gradually improved the quality of life and increased life expectancy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:**

 
 
• The British colonial administration did not prioritize healthcare and sanitation, resulting in poor health outcomes for the population.
 
• The lack of infrastructure and neglect of rural areas further exacerbated health issues.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Countries:**
 
 
• In 1947, India's life expectancy was significantly lower than that of developed countries, which averaged around 60-70 years during the same period.
 
• Countries with better healthcare systems and economic conditions had higher life expectancy rates.
 
 
 
• **Current Scenario:**
 
 
• As of 2023, India’s life expectancy has risen to over **70 years**, showcasing the progress in public health and socioeconomic development.
 
• Despite improvements, challenges such as **non-communicable diseases**, lifestyle disorders, and healthcare access disparities persist.
